chunks: And in the narration of Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm, from Abū ʿAbdillāh, from his father, peace be upon them both,
that ʿAlī عليه السلام was brought, in al-Kūfah, a man who had stolen a pigeon, so he did not cut off his hand, and he said: “I do not cut off for birds.”

key_terms.عَلِيّاً: Imam ʿAlī ibn Abī Ṭālib عليه السلام
key_terms.غِيَاثِ بْنِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ: the narrator Ghiyāth ibn Ibrāhīm in the chain
key_terms.يَقْطَعْهُ: to cut off his hand as the legal punishment

ai.seo_question: Does the hadd punishment for theft apply to stealing birds in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith reports a legal ruling from Imam ʿAlī عليه السلام regarding theft. It indicates that the hadd punishment of hand-cutting was not applied in the case of stealing a bird, showing that not every act of theft results in the same legal penalty.
